learning_outcomes.text: Learn how to formalize and solve real world problems and how to describe them to a computer.
Learn the basics of the C programming language.
Through lectures, students learn the fundamental knowledge of computer science and in particular of imperative programming and acquire the ability to understand programs written in C language.
Through practical exercises on the computer, the student is able to define sequential algorithms and to develop and verify programs using the C programming language.
Through the test, the student learns to quickly analyze part of a computer program evaluating what is essential in order for an algorithm to work.
Laboratory testing leaves complete freedom to choose the solution that is deemed suitable in order to comply with the proposed problem requirements.
The course and quiz tests require to develop considerable attention to the rigor in the language in referring to specific elements of the programs.
The described activities allow the student to acquire the methodological tools to continue their studies and to be able to arrange their own update.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and Information Representation
Information representation: positional number system, base 2, integer and fractional numbers
Bases 8 and 16, addition and subtraction of binary numbers, negative number representations, overflow and underflow
IEEE 754 standard, text representation, UNICODE
Architecture, Machine Language, and Assembly
Computer architecture: Von Neumann machine, the ADE8 educational processor
The concept of variable, managing multiple data, the concept of array, data addressing
Elementary C Constructs
From assembly to C: structure of a C program, the concept of data type, integer and floating-point types, variable definition, identifiers, initialization, read-only variables
Functions, the main function, assignment
Left and right associativity, expression types
The goto statement and labels, the if statement
High-level programming
The do-while and for constructs
Pointers
Memory allocation: malloc, free, and realloc
Advanced Constructs and Multi-file Source Usage
Allocating multiple data items: arrays
Accessing array elements with pointers and the square brackets operator
The C preprocessor
Structures in C: the struct directive
Defining structures and structure-type variables
Accessing structure members and passing a structure to a function
Defining new types: the typedef directive
Programming with Libraries and I/O
The standard library
Overview of math.h and string.h headers
The concept of a file as an abstraction of the underlying hardware
The stdio.h library
teaching_methods: Practical coding on computer in labs
assessment_rules: For each session, there are two tests: a theory test and a programming test. Both tests are evaluated with a maximum score of 33, and passing is achieved with a grade greater than or equal to 18. The written exam must be passed (grade>=18) to access the programming test. The final grade will be the weighted average (rounded to the nearest integer, 0.5 upwards) of the grades of the two tests, where the theory weighs 1 and programming weighs 2. The written test, once passed, remains valid until the start of the new course in September of the year following the start of the course.
